advice: Propose packing one 32-column slice of row-major B immediately before each column-panel computation, then reuse the existing full512 kernel on that panel. For panel p=0..15, pack `Bp[k*32+c] = B[k*512+p*32+c]` for k=0..511 and c=0..31 into 64 KiB scratch. Adapt both K loops to load from Bp with a 128-byte K stride and rewind 65536 bytes. Update the column-panel traversal to use Bp and write only columns `p*32..p*32+31` of C, while retaining the existing 64-row A packing and four-FMOPA FP32 order. All packing and scratch allocation stay inside gemm and are timed. Hypothesis: contiguous packed-B loads may improve the SME consumer enough to offset packing and per-panel setup; this is unverified. This differs from the measured full 1 MiB packed-B layout, which packed all sixteen panels, and from the measured panel32 calls and one-region wrapper.
risks: The B-panel packing, K-loop B stride and rewind, panel-to-C addressing, and outer traversal must agree. A stride or pointer error can read the wrong B values or leave C columns unwritten. Repacking B sixteen times may cost more than any consumer improvement. Keep FP32 arithmetic, ABI, fallback, tails, n<=0 behavior, and complete LIBXSMM BSD notice unchanged; preserve the existing allocation-failure fallback. Check the full GEMM against tolerance 0.002, including n=512, general sizes and tails, n<=0, output overwrite, and unchanged inputs. Then run fresh repeated paired controls with power source and settings unchanged, report score spread, and use the fixed promotion gates. Do not infer a packing or cache cause from noisy scores.
